newsitem.title: CHINA: HKFE rushes out timely red chip derivatives.
newsitem.headline: HKFE rushes out timely red chip derivatives.

text.p: The Hong Kong Futures Exchange (HKFE) has rushed to tailor derivative products on red chips to help risk management on the volatile stocks, its chief executive officer, Ivers Riley, said on Wednesday.
"We're seeing (that) the Stock Exchange has done a very good job of handling these particular stocks and now it's time for the risk management tools," he told a news conference.

The HKFE said earlier it would launch futures and options contracts on the Hang Seng China-Affiliated Corporations Index for red chips on September 12. The news came just three weeks and one day after the red chip index started trading on June 16.
"Yes, we are in a hurry," Riley said.
"When you bring these things, there are bigger chances of success when the market is crying out for (them) -- and the market is crying out for right now," he said.
Red chips, Hong Kong-incorporated companies with Chinese financial backing, have experienced high volatility in recent weeks.
"It's a little over twice the volatility of the Hang Seng Index at the present time," Riley said.
The pent-up volatility meant there was a great need for risk mangement, because the contracts would reduce volatility and increase volumes, he said.
Red chips index contracts would be traded on the exchange's automated trading system (ATS), partly because the HKFE aimed to make them available as soon as possible, he said.
"That is one good reason for moving into the electronic system because we don't have to worry about space," Riley said.
The success of the HKFE's Hang Seng Index futures and options contracts meant its physical trading floor lacked space for new products, he said.
At present, roughly 40 percent of HKFE members were on the electronic system, he said.
Riley said the new red chip products would bring almost all exchange members under the electronic system.
But the HKFE did not plan to switch its Hang Seng Index futures and options contracts to electronic trading.
"No exchange anywhere in the world has successfully moved a very liquid futures and options (product) from one environment to another environment," Riley said.
Dealing on Hang Seng Index futures and options takes place on the trading floor of the exchange.
Riley predicted a wave of opportunities in Asia for the HKFE over the next few months.
"We believe in Asia opportunities are going to be popping up all over the place in next several months," Riley said.
The HKFE wanted to respond to those opportunities as it had responded to the red chips, he added.
-- Alison Leung (852) 2843 6369
